source_text: Quodque ait, in Epicurum Tullius, manifesto argumento non dici illa subtiliter, quod cuiuscemodi homines passim sibi ea profitentur placere [n4] . Id isti, sicut omnia, more perverso, ad sapientiae putant testimonium pertinere.
pass_a_gloss: And what Cicero says against Epicurus, by a clear argument those things are not said with subtlety, because people of every sort everywhere profess that they please them. These men, as in all things, by a perverse custom, think that this belongs to a testimony of wisdom.
pass_b_english: Cicero says against Epicurus that there is clear evidence his teachings lack subtlety: people of every sort everywhere declare that they like them (Cicero, Tusculan Disputations 4.7). These people, perversely as in everything else, treat that as evidence of wisdom.

choices.why: Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
